title: A re-usable wave bioreactor for protein production in insect cells
author: Scholz, Suppmann

steps.title: Assemble bioreactor container
steps.instruction: Use a polycarbonate box (TECNIPLAST, 500 U Eurostandard Typ IV S, size 480 × 375 × 210 mm, volume 38 L) that is transparent and autoclavable at 121 °C (the first Cooper model was autoclaved 35 times without loss). Construct an in‑house lid from polycarbonate of the same size, seal it with a rubber‑foam layer and secure it to the base with six metal clamps on the four sides. Install seven ports with screw‑threaded connectors: two 13.5 Pg ports for optional pH or pO₂ sensors (not used), one wide‑mouth air‑outlet (5.4 cm inner diameter) capped with a C55 Silicon Cap (Hirschmann, VWR, Cat No 8905755) and protected with aluminium foil, and four 0.5 cm inner‑diameter ports for air inlet, aseptic sampling, medium fill and a wildcard.

steps.title: Install tubing and filters
steps.instruction: Fit the air‑inlet port with an Acro 50 0.2 µm PTFE filter (Pall, P/N 4151) and cover it with aluminium foil for autoclaving. Connect the sampling port to a Super Safe Sampler (Infors, Cat No 65373) using thin tubing (ID 2 mm, OD 4 mm). Set up the medium‑fill line with a long tubing (outside length 2.30 m, inside length 24 cm) attached via stainless‑steel quick connectors (Stäubli, Cat No RBE06.1806/IC/OD/JE and RBE06.7806/IC/JE) to a 1 L Schott bottle, pressure‑balanced by an Acrodisc CR 0.45 µm PTFE sterile filter (Pall). Use pharma‑compliant platinum‑cured silicone tubing (Applied Critical Fluids, Cat No I‑SA P60 40‑24‑88, ID 4.0 mm, OD 8.8 mm, wall 2.4 mm) suitable for peristaltic pumps and autoclavable.

steps.title: Sterilize bioreactor and bottle
steps.instruction: Autoclave the assembled bioreactor together with the connected Schott bottle at 121 °C, 15 psi for 20 min. After sterilization replace the Schott bottle with a medium reservoir or a 2 L culture bottle to be pumped into the reactor; this port can also be used for fed‑batch additions during cultivation.

steps.title: Grow insect cells
steps.instruction: Culture Sf9 cells (Life Technologies) or Hi5 cells (Gene Center, LMU Munich) in suspension using Ex‑Cell 420 medium (Sigma, Cat No 24420C). Maintain Sf9 at 1–5 × 10⁶ cells/mL and Hi5 at 0.2–5 × 10⁶ cells/mL; cell diameter should be ≈19 µm and viability >95 %. Monitor cell count, viability and diameter with a Vi‑cell XR cell counter (Beckman Coulter).

steps.title: Incubate cells in shaker
steps.instruction: Place cultures in Infors shaker incubators (50 mm rotating diameter) at 27 °C in Erlenmeyer EM or Fernbach FB glass flasks sealed with Silicon Caps (Hirschmann, VWR) using the following volume‑shaker settings: 30 mL in 250 mL EM at 120 rpm; 150 mL in 1 L EM at 120 rpm; 200–400 mL in 1.8 L FB at 90 rpm; 400 mL–1 L in 5 L EM at 90 rpm.

steps.title: Prepare baculovirus stocks
steps.instruction: Follow the Bac‑to‑Bac® protocol (Life Technologies) for bacmid transfection in Sf9 cells; harvest transfected cells after 3–5 days. Determine virus titer with the SF9‑ET easy‑titer cell line. Amplify virus in two successive passages to obtain Passage 1 and Passage 2 stocks, or generate Baculo‑Infected Insect Cells (BIIC) as described previously. Freeze BIICs at –80 °C for later protein expression and as virus storage.

steps.title: Infect cells for protein expression
steps.instruction: Adjust Hi5 and Sf9 cultures to 1 × 10⁶ cells/mL and infect with the virus stock or BIICs at dilutions typically ranging from 1:1 000 to 1:10 000. Proceed with protein production under the previously defined cultivation conditions.
